SMI closes 0.40 percent lower at 14,743.09 points before US midterm vote
sum: The Swiss Market Index ended Tuesday, November 3, 2026, lower after a hesitant session. The SMI closed at 14,743.09 points, a decline of 0.40 percent from the previous close of 14,802.52 points. The closing level and prior close are reported by MarketWatch; the contemporaneous market report from finanzen.ch, citing AWP, records the SIX session close at 17:30:38 local exchange time.

According to the AWP report carried by finanzen.ch, hopes for a de-escalation in the Middle East briefly supported European markets. Reports of new proposals from Qatari mediators aimed at preventing a renewed escalation in the conflict pushed Brent crude below 101 US dollars during the afternoon. Oil later recovered to above 103 US dollars, limiting the lasting effect of the earlier relief.

Political caution also shaped trading. Millions of voters in the United States went to the polls for the midterm elections, while investors awaited clearer indications of the result. The first meaningful projections were expected during the night into Wednesday, leaving market participants reluctant to take larger positions before the outcome became clearer.

Fourteen SMI constituents ended lower and six gained. Logitech fell 2.8 percent, while Geberit lost 2.2 percent. Galderma declined 1.3 percent after the company had announced the unexpected departure of its chief financial officer, who had held the position for only six months. Roche dropped 1.6 percent, and Nestle slipped 0.3 percent; Novartis finished almost unchanged, down 0.02 percent.

The declines were partly offset by gains in selected financial and industrial shares. ABB rose 1.6 percent, while Zurich Insurance advanced 0.3 percent and Swiss Life gained 0.6 percent. Partners Group added 0.5 percent. Outside the SMI, Clariant gained 1.4 percent after quarterly figures and positive comments from its chief executive, while Burckhardt Compression jumped 12.2 percent after its interim results exceeded market expectations.
The closing pattern points to a market balancing geopolitical signals, changing oil prices and company-specific news rather than following a single broad trend.

International General Insurance stock gets positive AM Best outlook
sum: International General Insurance Holdings enters its results week with a stronger external credit signal. On Thursday, October 29, 2026, AM Best revised the long-term issuer credit outlook for IGI to positive from stable while affirming the group's long-term issuer credit rating at "bbb" and the financial strength ratings of its operating subsidiaries at A (Excellent), according to Business Wire.

AM Best said the positive outlook reflects its expectation that IGI will continue to deliver strong operating performance relative to peers during a softer underwriting cycle. The agency also pointed to very strong risk-adjusted capitalisation, solid liquidity, a conservative investment portfolio and the absence of debt leverage.

The rating action gives investors a fresh balance-sheet reference point ahead of the company's scheduled financial update. AM Best expects modest medium-term growth as IGI maintains discipline in managing the underwriting cycle, but the outlook does not remove the need to monitor pricing, claims and reserve development in specialty insurance.

IGI plans to release third-quarter and first-nine-month 2026 results after the close of U.S. financial markets on Tuesday, November 3. The company will discuss the figures during an investor call on Wednesday, November 4, at 9:00 a.m. Eastern time, according to IGI.

The upcoming release will give investors the next reading on underwriting performance, investment income and capital returns after the first half of the year. Management's comments on conditions across specialty lines and reinsurance will be central to assessing whether the rating agency's positive medium-term view is translating into operating momentum.

IGI is a Bermuda-domiciled commercial insurer and reinsurer with Specialty Long-tail, Specialty Short-tail and Reinsurance segments. Its portfolio includes professional and financial lines, casualty, marine liability, energy, property, construction and engineering, political violence, marine cargo, general aviation and treaty reinsurance. The company operates internationally from underwriting locations including London, Bermuda, Malta, Dubai, Amman, Oslo, Kuala Lumpur, Casablanca and GIFT City in India.
